description: Kivi phonetic memory system evaluation cases. Designed before implementation. Each case specifies inputs, required memory state, expected output, expected decision, and the reason the system should give for its decision.

C1_correct_interventions.description: Cases where memory exists and should be applied. System must intervene.

cases.name: Basic person name correction via exact variant match
cases.asr_output: ask aditya to review the pull request
cases.formatted_output: Ask Aditya to review the pull request.
cases.expected_memory_aware_output: Ask Aaditya to review the pull request.

expected_decisions.reason: Exact variant match: 'Aditya' is a known variant of 'Aaditya'

cases.name: Product name correction — common misspelling
cases.asr_output: open the kiwi app on my laptop
cases.formatted_output: Open the Kiwi app on my laptop.
cases.expected_memory_aware_output: Open the Kivi app on my laptop.

expected_decisions.reason: Exact variant match: 'Kiwi' is a known variant of 'Kivi'

cases.name: Acronym correction — lowercase to correct casing
cases.asr_output: the nlp pipeline needs to be retrained
cases.formatted_output: The Nlp pipeline needs to be retrained.
cases.expected_memory_aware_output: The NLP pipeline needs to be retrained.

expected_decisions.reason: Exact variant match: 'Nlp' is a known variant of 'NLP'

cases.name: Multiple memories active — only the matched one applied
cases.asr_output: aditya works at sarvam on the kivi project
cases.formatted_output: Aditya works at Sarvam on the Kivi project.
cases.expected_memory_aware_output: Aaditya works at Sarvam on the Kivi project.

expected_decisions.reason: Exact variant match: 'Aditya' is a known variant of 'Aaditya'

cases.note: Sarvam is in memory but 'Sarvam' is not a variant of it — 'Saram' and 'Sarwam' are. The canonical form itself is not a variant. Token matches canonical directly so it is already correct — system must pass it through unchanged.

cases.name: Correction-sourced memory applied on next transcript
cases.asr_output: schedule a meeting with aditya tomorrow
cases.formatted_output: Schedule a meeting with Aditya tomorrow.
cases.expected_memory_aware_output: Schedule a meeting with Aaditya tomorrow.

expected_decisions.reason: Exact variant match: 'Aditya' is a known variant of 'Aaditya' (source: manual_correction)

cases.name: Technical term with unusual casing
cases.asr_output: we are migrating from tensorflow to pytorch
cases.formatted_output: We are migrating from TensorFlow to Pytorch.
cases.expected_memory_aware_output: We are migrating from TensorFlow to PyTorch.

expected_decisions.reason: Exact variant match: 'Pytorch' is a known variant of 'PyTorch'

C2_correct_abstentions.description: Cases where the system should NOT intervene. Abstaining is the correct behaviour.

cases.name: No memory exists — pass through unchanged
cases.asr_output: send the report to priya by friday
cases.formatted_output: Send the report to Priya by Friday.
cases.expected_memory_aware_output: Send the report to Priya by Friday.

cases.name: Phonetic match exists but token is not a known variant — abstain

expected_decisions.reason: Phonetic match found for 'Aaditya' but 'Adithya' is not a known variant. Abstaining to avoid incorrect correction.

cases.note: This is the most important abstention case. Adithya could be a different person. Without an exact variant match we must not apply.

cases.name: Memory suppressed — do not apply
cases.asr_output: ask aditya to check the logs
cases.formatted_output: Ask Aditya to check the logs.
cases.expected_memory_aware_output: Ask Aditya to check the logs.

expected_decisions.reason: Exact variant match found for 'Aaditya' but memory is suppressed. Abstaining.

cases.name: Token is canonical form itself — already correct, pass through

expected_decisions.reason: Token matches canonical form exactly — already correct, no intervention needed

cases.name: Common English word that phonetically matches a memory — must not over-correct
cases.asr_output: i had a kiwi for breakfast
cases.formatted_output: I had a kiwi for breakfast.
cases.expected_memory_aware_output: I had a kiwi for breakfast.

expected_decisions.reason: No phonetic match found — Double Metaphone encodes 'v' and 'w' differently (KF vs K). Transcript unchanged.

cases.note: This case confirms the system does not incorrectly over-correct. The algorithm limitation means the phonetic guard does not fire, but the outcome is still correct because no wrong correction is applied.

cases.name: Memory in needs_review status due to conflict — do not apply

expected_decisions.reason: Memory for 'Aaditya' is flagged as needs_review due to a conflict. Abstaining until resolved.

C3_learning_explicit.description: Cases that test the explicit input learning trigger.

cases.name: User explicitly adds a term — it is then applied
cases.setup: User calls POST /memory with canonical_form='Aaditya', category='person_name', variants=['Aditya']

expected_decisions.reason: Exact variant match: 'Aditya' is a known variant of 'Aaditya'

cases.name: User explicitly adds a term — phonetic hash is stored correctly
cases.setup: User calls POST /memory with canonical_form='Sarvam', category='org_name', variants=['Saram']
cases.verification: GET /memory should return the entry with a non-null phonetic_hash field

C4_learning_correction.description: Cases that test the manual correction learning trigger.

cases.name: User corrects transcript — memory created from diff

correction_input.original_formatted: Ask Aditya to review the pull request.
correction_input.corrected_text: Ask Aaditya to review the pull request.

cases.name: User corrects transcript — new variant added to existing memory

correction_input.original_formatted: Ask Adithya to join the call.
correction_input.corrected_text: Ask Aaditya to join the call.

cases.note: Adithya is a new bad form for the same person. It should be added as a variant, not create a new memory entry.

cases.name: Correction with no change — no memory created
cases.note: If the correction is identical to the original, no diff exists and no memory should be created.

C5_conflict_handling.description: Cases where two memories have conflicting phonetic profiles.

cases.name: Two entries with same phonetic hash — conflict flagged
cases.setup: User adds 'Aditya' (person A) and 'Aaditya' (person B) as separate canonical forms, both with variant 'Aditya'
cases.expected_behaviour: System detects phonetic hash collision on write and sets status to needs_review on the newer entry. Does not silently overwrite.

expected_api_response.message: Phonetic hash collision detected with existing entry. Entry created with status needs_review.

C6_user_control.description: Cases that test the user control and deletion endpoints.

cases.name: Delete a memory — hard delete with cascade
cases.setup: Memory for 'Aaditya' exists with variants and evidence log entries
cases.expected_behaviour: Entry deleted from vocabulary_entries. All variants deleted from vocabulary_variants. All evidence log entries deleted from evidence_log. GET /memory returns empty list.
cases.verification: After deletion, processing a transcript containing 'Aditya' should produce PASS decision, not APPLY.

cases.name: Suppress a memory — stops application without deleting
cases.setup: Memory for 'Aaditya' exists and is active
cases.expected_behaviour: Memory still exists in database. Processing transcript with 'Aditya' produces ABSTAIN decision with reason 'memory suppressed'.
cases.verification: GET /memory should still return the entry with status=suppressed.

cases.name: Reset — all memory cleared for user
cases.expected_behaviour: All entries, variants, and evidence logs deleted for the user. System behaves as if fresh for that user.
cases.verification: GET /memory returns empty list. Processing any transcript produces PASS decisions only.

cases.name: Empty transcript
All tokens match memories

expected_decisions.reason: Exact variant match: 'Aditya' is a known variant of 'Aaditya'
Exact variant match: 'Kiwi' is a known variant of 'Kivi'

cases.name: Punctuation stripped correctly before matching

expected_decisions.reason: Exact variant match after punctuation stripping: 'Aditya' is a known variant of 'Aaditya'

cases.note: The token 'Aditya.' (with trailing period) must be stripped to 'Aditya' before matching. The period must be reattached in the output.

cases.name: Multi-word canonical form handling
cases.note: Multi-word variants require the tokeniser to check adjacent token pairs, not just single tokens. This is a known complexity — if not implemented, document it as a known limitation.

primary: Precision — of all interventions made, what fraction were correct?
Recall — of all interventions that should have been made, what fraction were made?
Abstention correctness — of all abstentions, what fraction were correct (i.e. intervention would have been wrong)?
secondary: Evidence log completeness — does every decision have a logged reason?
reported_separately: Incorrect abstentions (false negatives — memory existed but was not applied when it should have been)
